items.sourceContext:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    name: test (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The full suite runs on Linux only: its runner, blind-unit confinement,
        # panel and file-permission tests are written for Linux (bubblewrap, POSIX
        # modes). Windows is proven by the focused tests in release-assets-check.yml
        # (installer, launchers, release assets); macOS is not a supported target.
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
    # Backstop so a hung run fails in bounded time instead of GitHub's 6h job cap.
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Default shallow (depth 1) clone: test/runner/coordination-p07-
          # migration-and-adversarial.test.mjs does `git archive <old ancestor
          # sha>` to materialize a real pre-schema-3 source tree, which needs
          # that commit's object present locally -- a shallow clone only has
          # the tip, so `git archive` failed "not a tree object" on all three
          # OSes. Full history, matching selector-plan's own checkout below.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Install Linux test tools
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        # Ubuntu 24.04 blocks unprivileged user namespaces via AppArmor, which
        # leaves bwrap installed but unable to build a sandbox; lift it so the
        # required-confinement tests really run here instead of skipping.
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y bubblewrap zsh
          if [ -e /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns ]; then
            sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
          fi
          bwrap --ro-bind / / -- true && echo "bwrap can build a sandbox"

      - name: Configure git identity for fixture repos
        run: |
          git config --global user.email "ci@example.com"
          git config --global user.name "CI"
          git config --global core.longpaths true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Build Rust release binaries for npm tests
        run: cargo build --locked --release --workspace

      # Full suite (docs/distribution-vision.md tsk-49r D1): already
      # includes test/install-packaging.test.mjs (the pack -> install -g ->
      # fgos init proof) and test/setup/doctor-fresh-run.test.mjs (the
      # fresh-runner fgos doctor proof, D4) on every OS in the matrix above.
      #
      # `mkdir -p test-results` runs first because `--test-reporter-destination`
      # never creates its own output directory: node --test opens the file for
      # writing at test-run start and crashes (ENOENT, exit 7, zero tests run)
      # the instant that directory is missing. `shell: bash` keeps the same
      # mkdir/test invocation on all three OSes in the matrix.
      - name: npm test (includes install-packaging matrix proof)
        id: run-tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          set +e
          npm test -- --test-reporter=spec --test-reporter-destination=stdout --test-reporter=junit --test-reporter-destination=test-results/full.xml
          code=$?
          echo "exit_code=$code" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          exit $code
        env:
          FORCE_COLOR: 1

      - name: Write test marker
        if: always()
        run: node scripts/write-test-marker.mjs --type full --xml test-results/full.xml --exit-code "${{ steps.run-tests.outputs.exit_code }}"
        env:
          JOB_STATUS: ${{ job.status }}

      - name: Upload full results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: full-results-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: test-results/
          retention-days: 14

  # `npm test` (scripts/run-tests.mjs, a portable `node --test` wrapper over
  # every discovered test/**/*.test.mjs) cannot see the Rust crate at all,
  # so until this job existed herdr-plugin had no automated
  # coverage anywhere — not locally, not here. It bit for real (tsk-1l9): a
  # one-line stage fixture change in src/app.rs broke an assertion in
  # src/ui.rs, and only a hand-typed `cargo test` caught it.
  #
  # One OS, not the matrix above: this crate is a local developer dashboard,
  # not a shipped cross-platform artifact, so per-OS proof would buy nothing
  # for the runtime cost. Widen it the day the crate is actually distributed.
  #
  # No toolchain action: ubuntu-latest ships a working Rust toolchain, so the
  # job needs no third-party action beyond the checkout this repo already
  # trusts. `rustup show` fails loudly if that ever stops being true, instead
  # of letting a missing toolchain read as a passing job.
  selector-plan:
    name: selector-plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      decision: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.decision }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm install

      - name: Generate plan
        id: plan
        run: |
          npm run test:ownership:lint
          npm run test:select:plan -- --base origin/main --plan-out selector-plan.json
          DECISION=$(node -p "require('./selector-plan.json').decision")
          echo "decision=$DECISION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Upload plan
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: selector-plan
          path: selector-plan.json
          retention-days: 14

  related:
    name: related
    needs: selector-plan
    if: needs.selector-plan.outputs.decision == 'related'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download plan
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: selector-plan

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm install

      - name: Build Rust host binary for tests
        run: cargo build --locked -p fgos

      - name: Run related tests
        id: run-tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p test-results
          set +e
          node scripts/test-select-run-plan.mjs --files-from selector-plan.json --test-reporter=spec --test-reporter-destination=stdout --test-reporter=junit --test-reporter-destination=test-results/related.xml
          code=$?
          echo "exit_code=$code" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          exit $code
        env:
          FORCE_COLOR: 1
          NODE_V8_COVERAGE: coverage/related

      - name: Write test marker
        if: always()
        run: node scripts/write-test-marker.mjs --type related --xml test-results/related.xml --plan selector-plan.json --exit-code "${{ steps.run-tests.outputs.exit_code }}"
        env:
          JOB_STATUS: ${{ job.status }}

      - name: Upload related results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: related-results
          path: test-results/
          retention-days: 14

  compare:
    name: compare
    needs: [selector-plan, related, test]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm install

      - name: Download artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: artifacts/

      - name: Download base artifact
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: |
          BASE_SHA=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          RUN_ID=$(gh run list --commit $BASE_SHA --workflow CI --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId' || true)
          if [ -z "$RUN_ID" ] || [ "$RUN_ID" == "null" ]; then
            RUN_ID=$(gh run list --branch ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }} --workflow CI --status success --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId' || true)
          fi
          if [ -n "$RUN_ID" ] && [ "$RUN_ID" != "null" ]; then
            gh run download $RUN_ID --name full-results-ubuntu-latest --dir artifacts/base-results/test-results || echo "Failed to download base artifact"
            if [ -f artifacts/base-results/test-results/full.xml ]; then
              mv artifacts/base-results/test-results/full.xml artifacts/base-results/test-results/base.xml
            fi
          fi
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Run compare
        run: npm run test:select:compare
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # test:select:compare exits before writing ledger.json when the
      # selector's own decision was 'full' (no comparison to make) -- the
      # file only exists on a genuine 'related' run. Without this upload,
      # every real compare ledger this repo ever produced was discarded the
      # instant the job container tore down: promoteRules (test-select-
      # promote.mjs) had no durable evidence to ever read, on any rule, ever.
      - name: Upload compare ledger
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: compare-ledger-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: ledger.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 90

  herdr-plugin:
    name: cargo test --locked (herdr-dashboard)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Show Rust toolchain
        run: rustup show && cargo --version

      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --locked --manifest-path herdr-dashboard/Cargo.toml

  # One OS, no toolchain action, same reasoning as the herdr-plugin job just
  # above: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu is the only target this track's Decisions
  # table covers (plan.md), and ubuntu-latest's preinstalled toolchain is
  # trusted the same way herdr-plugin's job already trusts it.
  rust-workspace:
    name: cargo (workspace)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Show Rust toolchain
        run: rustup show && cargo --version

      - name: cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: cargo test
        run: cargo test --locked --workspace

      - name: Install dependency auditor
        run: cargo install cargo-deny --locked --version 0.20.2

      - name: Audit locked dependencies
        run: cargo deny --config .github/cargo-deny.toml check advisories bans sources

  # Packages through the same script release.yml uses, so this proof and a release can
  # never differ. Built on ubuntu-22.04 like the release asset (see release-assets.yml).
  external-consumer:
    name: external consumer proof
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Show Rust toolchain
        run: rustup show && cargo --version

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build workspace (release)
        run: cargo build --locked --release --workspace

      - name: Check glibc ceiling of the shipped binaries
        run: scripts/check-glibc-ceiling.sh target/release/fgos target/release/fgctl

      - name: Build and package distribution assets
        run: node scripts/package-release-assets.mjs --version "v$(node -pe "require('./package.json').version")" --out dist

      - name: Run external consumer proof
        run: scripts/ci-external-consumer.sh --assets dist

  addon-reproducibility:
    name: addon reproducibility
    uses: ./.github/workflows/release-assets.yml
